title: Sections and local equality after sheafification on a site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf of sets on $\mathcal C$, and let $\theta^2:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F^\#$ be its sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. For every object $U$ and section $s\in\mathcal F^\#(U)$, there is a covering $(U_i\to U)_{i\in I}$ and sections $s_i\in\mathcal F(U_i)$ such that $s|_{U_i}=\theta^2(s_i)$ and, for every $i,j$, the pullbacks of $s_i$ and $s_j$ agree after a further covering of $U_i\times_UU_j$. Conversely, any such compatible local sections glue uniquely to a section of $\mathcal F^\#(U)$. In particular, if $p,q\in\mathcal F(U)$ have equal images in $\mathcal F^\#(U)$, then there is a covering $(U_i\to U)_{i\in I}$ on which $p|_{U_i}=q|_{U_i}$. This is Sites, Theorem Tag 00WB (theorem-plus) and Lemma Tag 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification).

source.place: Sites, Theorem Tag 00WB (theorem-plus), especially parts (2) and (4), and Lemma Tag 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification)

proof.text: Use the plus-construction realization of sheafification from [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-plus-theorem], which identifies the universal-property sheafification $\mathcal F^\#$ with $\mathcal F^{++}$. For $s\in\mathcal F^\#(U)$, the definition of the second plus construction gives a covering of $U$ on which $s$ is represented by sections of $\mathcal F^+$; refine each of those covering families by the first plus construction, so that on a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ the restriction of $s$ is represented by an actual section $s_i\in\mathcal F(U_i)$. On $U_i\times_UU_j$, equality of the two representatives in $\mathcal F^+$ means, by the common-refinement relation in the plus construction, that a further covering has equal pullbacks of $s_i$ and $s_j$. This is exactly the local representation and overlap condition of the statement; it is the construction in Sites, Lemma Tag 00WK.

source.place: Sites, Lemma Tag 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification), first paragraph, using the plus construction of Section 7.10

proof.text: Conversely, suppose that $\{U_i\to U\}$ and $s_i\in\mathcal F(U_i)$ satisfy the stated overlap condition. Their images $\theta^2(s_i)\in\mathcal F^\#(U_i)$ agree after pulling back to a covering of every $U_i\times_UU_j$: the further-cover equality of the $s_i$ is preserved by the sheafification map. Thus the family $(\theta^2(s_i))_i$ is descent data for the sheaf $\mathcal F^\#$, whose sheaf property and identification with $\mathcal F^{++}$ are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-plus-theorem]; the equalizer sheaf condition gives a unique $s\in\mathcal F^\#(U)$ restricting to it. The same uniqueness also shows that the section is independent of all refinements used to witness the overlap condition. This is the converse in Lemma Tag 00WK.

source.place: Sites, Theorem Tag 00WB, part (4), and Lemma Tag 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification), converse

proof.text: For the final clause, let $p,q\in\mathcal F(U)$ and assume $\theta^2(p)=\theta^2(q)$. Regard $p$ and $q$ first as the canonical sections of $\mathcal F^+(U)$. The separatedness assertion and injectivity of $\mathcal F^+\to\mathcal F^{++}$ in Theorem Tag 00WB(1)--(2), recorded as [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-plus-separated], imply that the two $\mathcal F^+$-representatives are equal. By the definition of equality in $\mathcal F^+$, each such equality has a covering refinement on which the restrictions of $p$ and $q$ agree in $\mathcal F$. Composing the refinements is a covering by the site axioms [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and on it $p|_{U_i}=q|_{U_i}$, as required.
